title: Dispatch GID 3: Stratum Images Follow Spectators Home
summary: Some witnesses now recognize rooms and people described by strangers at the showing.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Witnesses from Thursday’s demonstration have reported brief returns of the scenes they saw in the Lyceum. A clerk found the upward river reflected in his office window. Miss Morrow heard pages being turned in the empty archive she had seen. Neither event lasted long enough for a second witness to confirm it.

More troubling to the Institute are descriptions exchanged between people who had not spoken. The boy who saw a field of chairs recognized one of them in the sketch made by Dr. Saye, though she had described only the Lyceum. Dr. Saye says the chair stood in the space where she ought to have seen herself.

The Institute examined the unsold seat. Its upholstery bears a fresh impression. The mark remains even after the chair has been removed and stored overnight. Dr. Saye believes the instrument may have allowed something in the Stratum to observe the audience in return.

Dr. Halden disputes that conclusion. He calls the continuing images a sign that the demonstration trained the spectators’ perception. He has announced a second showing for a smaller group of scientists and journalists. Miss Marsh has asked him to wait for the Institute’s report.

Mabel Crain has supplied the newspaper with a plan of the exits. In the margin she marked a narrow passage between the last two rows. No such passage exists in the Lyceum. She says she saw it open when the warning was heard.
